title: Post-Training NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for Finance: More Accurate, Cost-Efficient Financial Credit Analysis
summary: AfterQuery and Hebbia post-trained the NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model on expert-written public credit tasks. Perfect solves on a 100-task held-out set rose from 47% to 74%.
body_markdown:
ANSWER: No. The $1,800,000 Restricted Payment is NOT permitted under Section 7.6(g) of the Amended Credit Agreement.


\[…\]


The First Amendment added a new condition (ii) imposing a 3.00:1.00 pro forma Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio cap on clause (g) payments. The First Amendment became effective on the First Amendment Effective Date (May 5, 2026) upon satisfaction of the conditions precedent in Section 5, and the Amended Credit Agreement governs the December 2026 payment.


\[…\]


Bottom line: No — the payment is not permitted under Section 7.6(g) because, although it is within the $2,500,000 aggregate cap and no Event of Default exists, the pro forma Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio of 3.25:1.00 exceeds the 3.00:1.00 maximum imposed by clause (g)(ii) as added by the First Amendment and Limited Waiver dated May 5, 2026.


\[…\]


2. However, the First Amendment and Limited Waiver to Credit Agreement, dated as of May 5, 2026 (the "First Amendment"), amended and restated Section 7.6(g) in its entirety. Section 2(f) of the First Amendment provides:


"(g) Holdings and its Subsidiaries may make Restricted Payments not otherwise permitted by one of the foregoing clauses of this Section 7.6; provided that (i) the aggregate amount of all such Restricted Payments made pursuant to this clause (g) shall not exceed $2,500,000 and (ii) after giving effect to such Restricted Payment, the Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio, on a Pro Forma Basis after giving effect such Restricted Payment, does not exceed 3.00:1.00;"
